geopolitics_summary: EU carbon market reform stalled; Russia oil sanctions deadline missed; Iran-Hormuz conflict raises crude volatility; France nuclear threatened by heat.

themes.headline: EU Commission to weaken carbon market, allowing industry more emissions
themes.why_it_matters: EUA price weakness ripples through power merit order. Lower carbon cost reduces fuel-switching incentive from gas to coal, pressuring power margins and TTF arb.

themes.headline: France nuclear forced offline by extreme heat, compressing supply
themes.why_it_matters: Nuclear shutdown reduces French baseload capacity mid-summer. Drives imports from Germany/Benelux; increases DA power prices and gas demand for peaking. Direct Day-Ahead spread impact.

themes.headline: EU-Russia oil sanctions deal collapses; price cap deadline end-July at risk
themes.why_it_matters: Failure to agree sanctions cap could allow Russian crude prices to spike, raising global crude cost. Higher oil feeds LNG economics via Brent-linked cargoes; indirectly tightens TTF via LNG arb pressure.

themes.headline: Middle East Strait of Hormuz disruptions persist; crude volatility elevated Q2
themes.why_it_matters: Continued Strait chokepoint tension sustains crude volatility and risk premium. Higher oil underpins LNG export economics; tightens global LNG-to-TTF arb, lifting European gas import cost.

themes.headline: Global LNG trade hit record 56.3 Bcf/d in 2025; US exports driving growth
themes.why_it_matters: Record US LNG capacity expansion increases supply optionality to Europe. If Middle East disruptions persist, EU may capture more US cargoes; competitive TTF pricing relief vs. geopolitical risk upside.

watchlist: EU ETS reform vote (Parliament/Council); outcome determines carbon floor and fuel-switch incentive.
Russia oil sanctions final deadline end-July; price cap agreement or cap ratchet up.
France nuclear return date as heat wave subsides; supply restoration risk to Day-Ahead spread.
Iran-Hormuz military escalation or de-escalation; crude price trajectory into August heating.
